ui.INTRO_BODY: This assessment helps adults decide what kind of care to seek. It does not confirm a diagnosis or check every possible cause. Answer about one main problem and the person being assessed.
ui.PROXY_NOTE: Answer about the person you are checking. If you cannot tell, choose “I’m not sure.” Questions use “you” to mean that person.
ui.MULTI_HELP: Select all that apply. “None of these” and “I’m not sure” cannot be combined with other answers.
ui.CHANGE_NOTE: Changing this answer may remove later answers that no longer apply.
ui.UNKNOWN_NOTE: Choose “I’m not sure” if you cannot tell. Please do not guess.
ui.EXIT_BODY: An unfinished assessment does not provide a care recommendation.
ui.RESULT_LIMIT: This is guidance based on your answers, not a diagnosis. It cannot rule out every serious cause.
ui.RESULT_LIMITED: This is a limited assessment. It recommends a next step but does not identify the cause.
ui.RESULT_UNCERTAIN: Some information remains uncertain, so a human clinical assessment is needed.
ui.LOCATION_NOTE: Your location helps us show suitable services. It does not change the medical urgency.
ui.NO_SLOT: No suitable appointment is available here within the recommended time. Use another appropriate local service; do not wait for a later platform appointment.
ui.SPECIALIST_HINT: Doctors in this field can evaluate your symptoms and advise on treatment
ui.EMERGENCY_TEXT: Please call emergency services (112 or 911) immediately or proceed to the nearest emergency room.
ui.CRISIS_TEXT: Please contact a 24/7 mental health crisis service or seek immediate emergency care.
ui.POISON_TEXT: Please contact poison control or emergency medical services immediately.
ui.PREVIOUS_RESULT_NOTE: This is the result from your last completed assessment
ui.ACTION_EMERGENCY: Call local emergency services (112 or 911) or proceed to the nearest emergency department immediately.
ui.ACTION_CRISIS: Contact a mental health crisis helpline or seek emergency medical evaluation immediately.
ui.ACTION_POISON: Contact poison control or emergency medical services immediately.
ui.ACTION_URGENT: Contact a suitable medical service now to be evaluated today.
ui.ACTION_MATERNITY: Contact a maternity or urgent care service for assessment today.
ui.ACTION_DOCTOR: Book an in-person consultation with a doctor.
ui.ACTION_PHARMACY: Consult a pharmacist or family doctor.
ui.ACTION_SELFCARE: Follow supportive self-care guidance and monitor for any changes.

U1.label: Emergency
U1.action: Call local emergency services or go to an emergency department now. Do not wait for a routine appointment.

U2.label: Urgent
U2.time: Contact an appropriate service now for assessment today.
U2.action: Contact the recommended service now. If it cannot assess you in time, use another local urgent clinical service.

U3.label: Soon
U3.time: Arrange assessment within 72 hours, unless a shorter deadline is shown.
U3.action: Arrange an assessment with the recommended service within the stated time. Seek help sooner if the listed changes occur.

U4.label: Routine
U4.time: Arrange a planned review within 1–2 weeks.
U4.action: Book a planned review. Seek earlier advice if symptoms change or become harder to manage.

U5.label: Self-care
U5.time: A consultation may not be needed now if symptoms continue to improve.
U5.action: Use the supportive steps below and watch for the listed changes. Contact a clinician if symptoms do not improve as described.

UNKNOWN.label: Clinical Assessment Needed
UNKNOWN.time: A consultation is recommended to evaluate symptoms.
UNKNOWN.action: Please consult a doctor to evaluate symptoms and discuss next steps.

C_ALLERGIC_RHINITIS.title: Possible nasal allergy
C_ALLERGIC_RHINITIS.why: The itching, sneezing and repeat exposure pattern may fit a nasal allergy.
C_ALLERGIC_RHINITIS.supportive: Avoid a trigger you already know affects you, where practical.

C_VIRAL_UPPER_RESPIRATORY_PATTERN.title: Possible viral upper respiratory infection
C_VIRAL_UPPER_RESPIRATORY_PATTERN.why: The recent combination of nose and throat symptoms may fit a common viral infection.
C_VIRAL_UPPER_RESPIRATORY_PATTERN.supportive: Rest as needed and drink your usual fluids unless a clinician has restricted them.

C_ACUTE_SORE_THROAT.title: Acute sore throat
C_ACUTE_SORE_THROAT.why: A short episode of mild throat pain can have several causes. This assessment cannot tell whether it is viral or bacterial.
C_ACUTE_SORE_THROAT.supportive: Choose comfortable drinks and avoid smoke or other throat irritants.

C_RESOLVING_POST_INFECTIOUS_COUGH_PATTER.title: Possible cough following a recent infection
C_RESOLVING_POST_INFECTIOUS_COUGH_PATTER.why: A cough that followed a cold and is improving may be part of recovery.
C_RESOLVING_POST_INFECTIOUS_COUGH_PATTER.supportive: Avoid smoke and other triggers that make the cough worse.

C_MIGRAINE_PATTERN.title: Possible migraine pattern
C_MIGRAINE_PATTERN.why: The combination of headache characteristics and associated symptoms may fit migraine.
C_MIGRAINE_PATTERN.supportive: Rest in a comfortable, quiet space and follow an existing clinician-agreed care plan.

C_TENSION_HEADACHE_PATTERN.title: Possible tension-type headache
C_TENSION_HEADACHE_PATTERN.why: The pressure-like pain on both sides and its relationship to activity may fit a tension-type headache.
C_TENSION_HEADACHE_PATTERN.supportive: Take a break from activities that increase discomfort and keep regular sleep and meal routines.

C_CONSTIPATION_PATTERN.title: Possible constipation
C_CONSTIPATION_PATTERN.why: Hard or less frequent stool with straining may fit constipation.
C_CONSTIPATION_PATTERN.supportive: Keep a regular toilet routine. If comfortable, stay gently active and gradually include more fibre in normal meals. Follow any fluid restriction.

C_REFLUX_PATTERN.title: Possible acid reflux
C_REFLUX_PATTERN.why: Familiar burning after meals with a sour taste may fit acid reflux.
C_REFLUX_PATTERN.supportive: Try smaller meals and avoid lying down soon after eating. Avoid foods you already know trigger the symptoms.

C_ACUTE_GASTROENTERITIS_PATTERN.title: Possible acute gastroenteritis
C_ACUTE_GASTROENTERITIS_PATTERN.why: The short episode of loose or watery stool may fit a stomach or bowel infection. The cause cannot be confirmed here.
C_ACUTE_GASTROENTERITIS_PATTERN.supportive: Take small drinks as tolerated and rest. Keep within any fluid limit set by your clinician.

C_LOWER_UTI_PATTERN.title: Possible lower urinary tract infection
C_LOWER_UTI_PATTERN.why: The combination of burning, new night-time urination or cloudy urine may fit a lower urinary infection.
C_LOWER_UTI_PATTERN.supportive: Drink normally within any existing fluid limits while arranging the recommended assessment.

C_POSSIBLE_SKIN_INFECTION.title: Possible skin infection
C_POSSIBLE_SKIN_INFECTION.why: Painful, hot or swollen skin can occur with an infection or another condition and needs clinical assessment.
C_POSSIBLE_SKIN_INFECTION.supportive: Omit this section; arranging assessment takes priority.

C_HIVES_PATTERN.title: Possible hives
C_HIVES_PATTERN.why: Raised itchy patches that appear and fade may fit hives.
C_HIVES_PATTERN.supportive: Avoid a trigger you already know affects you and avoid scratching the area.

C_CONTACT_DERMATITIS_PATTERN.title: Possible contact dermatitis
C_CONTACT_DERMATITIS_PATTERN.why: Dry, itchy skin where contact occurred may fit irritation or contact dermatitis.
C_CONTACT_DERMATITIS_PATTERN.supportive: Avoid the suspected contact where practical. Do not deliberately re-expose yourself to test it.

C_SCIATICA_PATTERN.title: Possible sciatica pattern
C_SCIATICA_PATTERN.why: Pain spreading from the buttock down one leg may fit irritation of a nerve. An examination is needed.
C_SCIATICA_PATTERN.supportive: Keep moving gently within comfort and avoid prolonged bed rest.

C_MECHANICAL_BACK_PAIN_PATTERN.title: Possible mechanical low-back pain
C_MECHANICAL_BACK_PAIN_PATTERN.why: Local pain linked to activity and movement may fit a common mechanical back-pain pattern.
C_MECHANICAL_BACK_PAIN_PATTERN.supportive: Continue comfortable daily movement and avoid prolonged bed rest.

C_MUSCLE_OVERUSE_PATTERN.title: Possible muscle overuse
C_MUSCLE_OVERUSE_PATTERN.why: Local pain after repeated or unfamiliar activity may fit muscle overuse.
C_MUSCLE_OVERUSE_PATTERN.supportive: Temporarily ease off the activity that caused the discomfort and use comfortable movement.

escalations.E_B01: Get emergency help for severe breathing difficulty, inability to swallow saliva, more than a few spots or streaks of coughed-up blood, or blood with breathing difficulty, a very fast heartbeat or chest/upper-back pain. Seek same-day advice for a few small blood spots or streaks, new breathlessness or marked deterioration. Arrange review if a sore throat is not improving after 7 days or a cough lasts over 21 days.
escalations.E_B02: Get emergency help for a sudden extremely severe headache, new weakness or speech difficulty, a seizure, loss of vision, or headache with fever and a stiff neck. Seek earlier advice if the headache changes or becomes difficult to manage.
escalations.E_B03: Get emergency help for sudden or severe abdominal pain, vomiting blood, black tar-like stool, or inability to pass stool and wind. Seek same-day advice if pain persists, returns, worsens, becomes focused in one area, or occurs with pregnancy or new urinary symptoms.
escalations.E_B04: Get emergency help for blood or green vomit or sudden severe pain. Seek same-day advice if you cannot keep drinks down, pass much less urine, see blood in stool, or deteriorate. Seek same-day advice if vomiting lasts beyond 48 hours or diarrhoea beyond 7 days.
escalations.E_B05: Get emergency help if you cannot pass urine or develop confusion or unusual drowsiness. Seek same-day advice for fever or chills, pain below the ribs in the back, blood in urine, worsening symptoms or no improvement after the existing 48-hour care period.
escalations.E_B06: Get emergency help for sudden mouth, tongue or throat swelling, breathing difficulty, or a painful blistering rash with sores inside the mouth, eyes or genitals, or sudden faintness/confusion with a skin reaction. Seek same-day advice for painful, hot and swollen skin, deep swelling, marked illness or a new rash after a medicine change.
escalations.E_B07: Get emergency help for new bladder or bowel control problems, numbness around the genitals or anus, or symptoms in both legs. Seek same-day advice for new weakness, feverish illness or sudden severe or rapidly worsening pain. Arrange review if pain is not improving by 14 days.
escalations.E_B08: Get emergency help for a deformed limb, new loss of sensation or inability to bear weight, or a cold pale painful limb with loss of function. Seek same-day advice for a hot swollen joint or one-sided limb swelling. Arrange review if pain is not improving by 14 days.
escalations.E_L01: Get emergency help if chest discomfort becomes persistent or occurs with breathlessness, sweating or faintness, if breathing becomes severe, or if you do not recover normally after fainting.
escalations.E_L02: Get emergency help for sudden weakness, speech difficulty, new severe imbalance or confusion, even if a sudden neurological symptom later stops. Get immediate assessment for weakness getting worse in both arms or both legs over four weeks. Seek same-day advice for other new weakness or severe unexplained dizziness.
escalations.E_L03: Get emergency help for new confusion, severe breathing difficulty, mottled or blue-grey skin with illness, or a non-fading rash. Seek same-day advice for worsening illness, dehydration or no improvement by 48 hours from the start of the fever.
escalations.E_L04: Get emergency help for sudden loss of vision or severe eye pain. Seek same-day advice for new blurred or double vision, flashes, a moving shadow or a painful light-sensitive eye.
escalations.E_L05: Get emergency help for mouth or face swelling affecting breathing or swallowing, eye involvement or inability to open the mouth. Seek same-day advice for sudden hearing loss, increasing ear swelling or suspected dental infection.
escalations.E_L06: Get emergency help for severe or worsening pelvic pain, faintness, shoulder-tip pain, heavy bleeding with pelvic symptoms, or sudden severe testicular pain. Seek same-day advice for pelvic symptoms with possible pregnancy, fever or new urinary difficulty.
escalations.E_L07: Do not wait for symptoms after a potentially harmful exposure. Contact the recommended emergency or poison-information service now.
escalations.E_L08: Get emergency help for uncontrolled bleeding, new neurological symptoms, a deformed or numb limb or a cold discoloured limb. Seek same-day advice if pain or swelling worsens, movement becomes difficult or the wound may need prompt treatment.
escalations.E_L09: If you may act to harm yourself or someone else, cannot stay safe, or have taken an overdose or caused serious injury, contact local emergency services now.
escalations.E_L10: If symptoms become severe, worsen quickly or make basic activities difficult, seek urgent human medical advice. This assessment has not checked every possible cause.
